scenes.headline: Working with CSV
scenes.subtitle: Reading and writing comma-separated text files.
scenes.narration: CSV is a simple text format, and Spark reads and writes it with options for headers, schema, and delimiters.

scenes.headline: CSV essentials
items: header option treats the first row as column names
inferSchema samples data to detect types
An explicit schema is faster and safer
Options set delimiter, quote, and null handling
scenes.narration: The header option treats the first row as column names, and inferSchema samples the data to detect types. An explicit schema is faster and safer, and further options control the delimiter, quoting, and null handling.

scenes.headline: Reading CSV with a schema
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, DoubleType

schema = StructType([
    StructField("name", StringType()),
    StructField("amount", DoubleType())])
df = spark.read.option("header", True).schema(schema).csv("/data/sales.csv")
scenes.narration: We define an explicit schema with a string name and a double amount, then read the CSV supplying that schema and a header option. Providing the schema avoids an extra data-scanning pass and prevents Spark from guessing types incorrectly.

scenes.text: Supply a schema for CSV in production — inference is slow and can be wrong.
scenes.narration: In production always supply a schema for CSV, since inference forces an extra scan of the file and can still guess wrong.
